slices.focus: After the typhoon failure, Ayaka rebuilds her pilot into a leaner recovery package with laminated backup cards, blunt ownership rules, and a narrower essential-freight definition.
slices.summary: Ayaka does not abandon the work after the typhoon collapse. She rebuilds it into a stripped-down recovery package using incident photos, phone timestamps, and a marked-up terminal map. Key elements: laminated backup notice cards for common disruption messages, blunt written ownership rules for passenger and cargo communication, and a narrower essential-freight definition tied to concrete household impact (medicine timing, basic groceries). She faces mixed reactions but refuses to soften the core argument.
open_loops: Narrower essential-freight definition may leave legitimate needs unprotected
Laminated cards depend on caches being maintained and stocked
Ownership rules may be resisted by staff who prefer flexible roles
